 J U D G M E N T
This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .20,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 29.06.2022 at about 07.00 to 07.30 a.m., when he was riding his Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-KC- 9623 near Yeliyur Gate, Vijayapura Hobli,
Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-23-AZ-4330, driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against petitioner's motor cycle.

Due to the accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter, he was shifted to Siridi Sai Hospital, Devanahalli and then to Bengaluru Baptist Hospital, Hebbal, Bengaluru,
wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.

Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as X-ray Technician work in Lavender Multy Speciality Hospital Pvt Ltd., at Bengaluru and getting a salary of .20,000/- per month.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver.

The respondents, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle,
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal and hence he has been placed ex-parte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed the written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.2 denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.2 also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondent No.2 contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further respondent No.2 admits the issue of policy bearing No.2804033121P105741213 in favour of first respondent with respect to lorry and contended that the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
Further contended that the rider of motor cycle was riding his motor cycle without using headgear (helmet) and without following traffic rules and caused the accident.
The amount claimed by petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the petition.
5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office has framed the following:

ISSUES 1. Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 29.06.2022 at about 07.00 to 07.30 a.m., near Yeliyuru Gate, Vijayapura Hobli, Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, when he was riding a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-KC-9623, due to the rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-23-AZ-4330 by its driver?

Rakesh R vs Rathinam K on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122835002/
2
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?

6. In order to prove the contention of petition, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and examined Dr.S.A.Somashekara working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.17 and closed their side of evidence.
The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.

7. Heard the arguments of both side and perused the materials available on record.
8.

The petitioner contended that on 29.06.2022 at about 07.00 to 07.30 a.m., accident occurred near Yeliyur Gate, Vijayapura Hobli, Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, when petitioner was riding his Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-KC-9623, due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-23-AZ-4330 by its driver in which he sustained grievous injuries.
10. In order to prove rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-23-AZ-4330 by its driver, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
In the chief examination, PW.1 deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver the accident occurred.
On perusal of cross-examination of PW.1, nothing has been elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disprove the case of petitioner.

Nothing to dispute the contention of petitioner related to accident and negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle, could be elicited during the cross examination of PW.1.
11.
Further, in order to prove accident, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.1 & 2, FIR and first information.
On perusal of Ex.P.2, first information statement, one Sri.Gajendra S/o.Thammareddy has lodged a complaint with police on 29.06.2022.
The police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.

The petitioner also furnished spot mahazar & sketch which are marked as Rakesh R vs Rathinam K on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122835002/
3 Ex.P.3 & 4.
The said documents disclose that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said documents.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that the facts, as described in the mahazar and sketch, are contrary to the actual facts at the place of accident.
12. Further, the petitioner furnished Ex.P.5, IMV Report, wherein the damages caused to the vehicles are mentioned.
The said document discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The IMV report discloses the aspect of damages caused to the offending vehicle.
The driver or owner of the offending vehicle not provided satisfactory explanation regarding the manner in which damages are caused to the vehicle.
The said document indicates involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
Ex.P.6 is the Wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner in the road traffic accident.
The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.338, 279, 304(A) of IPC as per Ex.P.8.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
13. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The respondents placed nothing before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
On perusal of records, it discloses that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P8, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-23-AZ-4330 by its driver and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income Rakesh R
vs Rathinam K

on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122835002/
4 during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.
i) Towards injury, pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.

In order to prove the injuries sustained, the petitioner produced Wound certificate marked at Ex.P.6,
wherein it discloses the injuries sustained by petitioner and the injuries are grievous in nature.

As per the materials on record, the petitioner has taken treatment at the hospital as an inpatient and he has produced Ex.P7 - Discharge Summary issued by Bengaluru Baptist Hospital and also examined Dr.S.A.Somashekara as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P16 & 17.
PW.2/doctor has deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of permanent physical disability, to the right lower limb at 54% and to the whole body at 27%.
By considering the injuries and facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that the compensation of .50,000/- appears just and reasonable towards pain and suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at Hospital.
The petitioner has produced medical bills for a sum of .2,85,485/- marked at Ex.P.9 and medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P.10.
Bill number 1 at Ex.P9 is the final bill issued by Bangalore Baptist Hospital.
The said bill discloses the total amount to be .2,33,012/-.
The said document also discloses the aspect of payment of .2,09,691/- by Niva Bupa Health Insurance Ltd.

The aspect of payment of .2,09,691/-
is mentioned in detailed final bill also which is produced at bill No.2.
The said documents disclose the aspect of payment of bill amount by the insurance company.
No materials are placed by petitioner to show that remaining amount is paid by him.

The documents furnished by petitioner clearly disclose the aspect of payment of final bill of .2,09,621/- by Niva Bupa Health Insurance Ltd and as such, the petitioner is not entitled to the amount mentioned in Ex.P9, final bill.
Further, the petitioner furnished inpatient pharmacy credit bill.
The amount mentioned in the said bills is included in the final bill.
The said aspect could be depicted from the detailed final bill furnished by petitioner.
The detailed final bill apparently discloses the aspect of inclusion of amounts mentioned in the credit pharmacy bills.
As such, the petitioner is not entitled to the amount mentioned in pharmacy bills.
The petitioner furnished out-patient bills amounting to .35,571/- and I.P settlement voucher for .22,891/- which total amounts to .58,462/-.
The said amount appears to have been paid by the petitioner.
The materials on record do not disclose the aspect of payment of said bill amount by the insurance company.
As such, the petitioner is entitled to said amount of .58,462/-.
So, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .58,462/- appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges:
On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 29.06.2022 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital.
On perusal of evidence, the petitioner got admitted as an inpatient at Hospital as he has sustained injuries.
During the time of treatment the petitioner might have required good food and extra nourishment.

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.7 - Discharge Summary, wherein it discloses that Rakesh R vs Rathinam K on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122835002/
5
the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient from 29.06.2022 to 06.07.2022 i.e., for a period of 08 days

. Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .500/- per day for 08 days to a sum of .4,000/- appears just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.
(iv) Towards Conveyance:

The petitioner is the resident of Anandagiri Extension, Bengaluru North, H.A.Farm,
Bengaluru and he got admitted to hospital for treatment.
In order to prove this aspect the petitioner has produced Discharge Summary marked at Ex.P.7.
The petitioner might have incurred expenses towards the conveyance.
Considering the injuries and facts of the case, the tribunal is of view that the compensation of .10,000/- appears just and proper towards conveyance charges.
(v) Towards loss of income during treatment:

The petitioner contended that he was working as a X- ray Technician in Lavender Multy Speciality Hospital Pvt Ltd. and getting salary of .20,000/- per month.
In order to prove his income, the petitioner has not produced any documents.

sentences.text: The petitioner not furnished satisfactory materials to show that he was earning .20,000/- per month.
The petitioner not furnished materials to substantiate his contention related to his occupation and income.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, notional income of petitioner is to be considered.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as .15,500/-.
On perusal of record, it appears that petitioner might not have attended his work for some time due to accidental injuries.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .20,000/- towards loss of income during treatment.
(vi) Towards Loss of future earning capacity:
The petitioner contended that due to accident, he got admitted as an inpatient at the hospital for availing the treatment and sustained permanent disablement.
The petitioner also examined Dr.S.A. Somashekara, working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru as PW.2.
PW.2/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess disabilities.

The doctor deposed that petitioner has sustained right femur shaft type 1 open fracture, left hand 3rd metacarpal fracture,
T8 compression fracture, B/L inferior pubic ramii fracture and left superior pubic ramus fracture and liver laceration and underwent surgery in the form of CRIF with femur IMIL Nailing with wound debridement on 29.06.2023, left 3rd MC fracture closed reduction and perentaneous K-wire on 04.07.2022 and later discharged.

Further on examination of disability assessment, the petitioner stated to have Rakesh R vs Rathinam K on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122835002/
6 complained of pain and difficulty in walking and climbing stairs, persistent low back ache, pain and difficulty in using left hand, inability to squat and sit cross legged,
inability to bend for wary and lift weight.

Further, recent X- ray reveals united fracture of right femur with implants in situ, united fractures of pubic ramii, T8 compression fracture malunited and malunited fracture base of 3rd metacarpal left hand.
The doctor examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and assessed the disability to the right lower limb at 54% and to the whole body at 27%.
In order to prove the disability, doctor has produced Ex.P.16 & 17 i.e., clinical notes and X-ray.
PW.2 not stated that the petitioner could not be able to do his routine activities in a normal way.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the petitioner to show that the petitioner is unable to do any work at all.
The injuries sustained by petitioner do not appear to cause much problem in doing his activities.
By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do his work with difficulty.
As per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another and considering facts and circumstances of the case, the functional disability is assessed at 20%.

sentences.text: In order to prove age, the petitioner produced Ex.P.14 & 15 - Notarized copies of Aadhaar Card and Driving License, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 04.05.1996.
The accident occurred on 29.06.2022, so the age of petitioner 26 years at the time of alleged accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier.
As per Smt.Sarla Verma case the multiplier applicable is '17'.
As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of his gross income.

sentences.text:
Hence, future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under :
Annual Income before accident : (.15,500/- x 12) = .1,86,000/-
 Loss of future earning p.a. (20% of prior annual  income) = .37,200/-.

Multiplier applicable with reference to age - 17 Loss of future earnings - (.37,200/- x 17) = .6,32,400/-.
The petitioner is entitled for .6,32,400/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
(vii) Deprivation of Future Amenities:- The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he is unable to do his day- today activities as earlier.

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of Rakesh R vs Rathinam K on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122835002/
7 future amenities.

(viii) Towards Future Medical Expenses:
The doctor/PW.2 has opined that the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implants which would cost around .40,000/-.
The petitioner not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to substantiate the said contention.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal in order to ascertain the expenses that may be incurred for the surgery for removal of implants.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case .25,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future medical expenses.

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

sentences.text: 17. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents No.1 and 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-23-AZ-4330 by its driver.
There appears to be no dispute related to ownership of respondent No.1 pertaining to the offending vehicle.

The materials on record disclose that the vehicle was having valid and effective policy of insurance and Rakesh R vs Rathinam K on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122835002/
8
the driver of offending vehicle was having valid and effective licence at the time of accident.
So, the respondent No.1 & 2, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
18. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .8,09,862/- (Rupees Eight Lakhs Nine Thousand Eight Hundred and Sixty Two only) with interest at 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and  severally liable to pay compensation to  petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 40% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank and the remaining 60% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of her Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.

Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to his account after expiry of three years period of deposit,
without waiting for further order of court.
The Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
